title: Doha, Hormuz and New York: The Economic Stakes of a Possible Iran–US Diplomatic Opening
text:
Doha, Hormuz and New York: The Economic Stakes of a Possible Iran–US Diplomatic Opening"

"Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi’s stop in Doha before travelling to New York comes at a particularly sensitive moment for the region."

"Qatar has been maintaining communication with both Tehran and Washington, while the Strait of Hormuz remains under severe pressure and commercial shipping is still far below normal levels."

"The important question is not simply whether Iran and the US will meet."
"The more consequential question for businesses and markets is whether diplomacy can produce a measurable change on the ground — particularly in shipping through Hormuz, energy flows, insurance costs and sanctions-related risks."

"From an economic perspective, the distinction between a diplomatic signal and a real change in conditions is critical."

"Oil markets have already shown how quickly expectations can change. At the same time, Qatar’s LNG sector and regional supply chains remain exposed to prolonged disruption."

"For companies operating in the Gulf, energy, logistics or regional trade, the next stage may therefore be less about political statements and more about what happens to actual shipping and energy flows."

"I have prepared a detailed analysis looking at the Iran–Qatar–US channel, Hormuz and the wider economic implications from the perspective of an Iranian analyst."

"The full report is attached below."
